description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:140 declares:

    pub const AIA_MAX_DEPTH: usize = 5;

Being `pub const`, this is part of the API surface in two ways:

1. **Value-level dependency.** A caller can write `[u8; pkix_chain::AIA_MAX_DEPTH]`, `static SCRATCH: [u8; AIA_MAX_DEPTH] = [...]`, or branch on `if depth == AIA_MAX_DEPTH`. The literal value `5` is locked in: a maintainer who later decides 5 is wrong (e.g. raises to 8 to cover an exotic enterprise PKI, or lowers to 3 because real-world cross-signed roots never need more than 3) cannot change it without a SemVer-breaking change of the constant value. `pub const`s are exempt from `#[non_exhaustive]`-style soft compatibility — any change to the value can break a caller's `const`-context use.

2. **Visibility-level dependency.** Callers can pattern-match on `Error::AiaDepthExceeded` and reference `AIA_MAX_DEPTH` in user-facing diagnostics ("AIA fetching gave up after {AIA_MAX_DEPTH} hops"). That binds pkix-chain to expose this internal tuning parameter as a stable identifier.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE CALLER: a caller building a defensive log line ("AIA depth limit ({AIA_MAX_DEPTH}) reached, dropping connection") gets a different log message on every pkix-chain minor bump that touches the value. There is no `#[deprecated]` story for the value of a `pub const` — only for the name.

OPTIONS (any one resolves the lock-in):

(a) Make it `pub(crate) const AIA_MAX_DEPTH: usize = 5;` and have `Error::AiaDepthExceeded`'s Display impl print the depth value at runtime (it already does — line 257). External callers neither need nor benefit from referencing the constant by name; the error variant alone is sufficient signal.

(b) Replace with `pub fn aia_max_depth() -> usize { 5 }`. Function returns are not const-context callable, so the literal-baking-in hazard is gone; future tunings are non-breaking.

(c) Keep `pub` but bind it explicitly to the variant: `Error::AiaDepthExceeded(usize)` carrying the depth at which it triggered. The const becomes informational, not normative.

The current rustdoc (lines 127-140) frames AIA_MAX_DEPTH as a tunable-but-fixed default. The framing argues for (b) or (c). PKIX-sqek.16 separately defends the cap's existence against future contributors who would make it configurable; this finding is about WHO can see the value, not whether the cap exists. The two are orthogonal.

This is a 0.x architectural-completeness call: per AGENTS.md's "Project phase and decision framing," picking the right shape now is free; picking it after 1.0 ships requires a major bump.
title: AIA_MAX_DEPTH is a pub const at value 5; callers can depend on the literal value forever
